solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Censure swapping diamonds for good evening wear

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another signals that one letter is replaced by another

parts.note: a dressing-down is a stern telling-off
D is the card abbreviation for the diamonds suit

explanation.surface: A rebuke in which jewels are exchanged for a smart outfit to wear at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping diamonds for good' changes the D of DRESSING DOWN to a G.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing gown is a robe put on in the evening over nightclothes, hence a garment for late hours.

clue.text: Diminish three consecutive semitones

definitions.meaning: to reduce or let down, as a tyre loses air
the notes D, E flat and E follow each other a semitone apart

explanation.surface: A musical instruction to reduce something by a run of semitones.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into the note names D, E FLAT and E, a chromatic run.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflate is to reduce or shrink something, as a balloon empties of air.

clue.text: Looks longingly at fashionable range

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it with desire
hot means trendy, in demand

explanation.surface: Someone gazes wistfully at a stylish collection of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshot is the distance within which one can see, the range of sight.

clue.text: Abrasive doctor appears to control new department

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the next pieces, controlling them from either side
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harsh physician seems to be taking charge of a newly created hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor reads as a physician but is the anagram signal: it shuffles the next word into SAPAPER, and 'to control' has that hold N and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandpaper is rough paper used to smooth wood, an abrasive material.

clue.text: Behind in a test to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Coming last, in an exam, partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nates is the anatomical Latin for the buttocks, the bottom one sits on.

clue.text: Smuttier writer's one probing king and his daughter

indicators.note: something that probes pokes into the middle, so these letters go inside

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the royal cipher of King George
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the daughter of King George VI
the writer's means the writer is, which the setter says as I'M
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A writer's work investigates a monarch and his daughter, rather like King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probing' puts the writer's pieces inside. The royal ciphers fit because King George VI's daughter was Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimier means dirtier or more soiled, matching smuttier in its literal sense of sootier.

clue.text: At sea, use it in worst extremes?

definitions.text: At sea, use it in worst extremes?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the outer pair
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
at sea means confused, so the letters of the next words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice to wear something out on the water when conditions are at their harshest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' jumbles USE IT to make ETSUI, which goes 'in' W and T, the 'extremes' of worst. The whole clue also describes the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A wetsuit is the rubber garment divers and surfers wear in cold water, ideal for bad sea conditions.

clue.text: Private place for stylus when disc's finished

definitions.meaning: said in confidence, not for publication

definitions.text: place for stylus when disc's finished
definitions.meaning: the needle of a record player is lifted clear of the vinyl at the end

explanation.surface: A confidential note about where to rest the needle once the LP stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made off the record are confidential and not to be quoted, so private.

clue.text: Rugby team play in fine fettle, apart from second half

indicators.note: play suggests loose movement, so these letters are rearranged
leaving out the second half of a word keeps only its first half

explanation.surface: A rugby side plays well, in good condition, except after half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from second half' leaves FET from fettle; 'play' rearranges FINE + FET.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union side has fifteen players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Where to wash and dry one of the Tweedle brothers?

definitions.text: Where to wash and dry one of the Tweedle brothers?

parts.words: Where to wash and dry one of the Tweedle brothers?
parts.note: Tweedledum and Tweedledee are a twin pair in Through the Looking-Glass, and a tub is for bathing; the phrase also names a washing machine

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about bathing one of Lewis Carroll's identical brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: A twin tub is an old-style washing machine with one drum for washing and one for spin-drying.
explanation.definitionFit: The appliance has two drums side by side, one to wash clothes and one to spin them dry.

clue.text: When emotions are highest, book place for Grease

parts.note: an oiling point is the spot on a machine where lubricant is applied

explanation.surface: At the height of feeling, someone reserves a seat for the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: Grease looks like the 1970s musical; it is lubricant, and 'place for' it is an oiling point.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling point is the idiom for the moment anger or excitement can no longer be held in.

clue.text: Retired bard drinks a quiet cuppa here

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so these letters go inside
retired means drawn back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a bard is a poet
SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A poet in retirement sips a peaceful cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reverses POET to TEOP, which 'drinks' A + SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A teashop is a small café where tea is served, so where one has a cuppa.

clue.text: Spurs limit us in a different configuration

indicators.note: a new configuration is a rearrangement of the given letters

explanation.surface: Tottenham's football team restricts us by playing in a new formation.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs looks like the Tottenham Hotspur football club; it means incentives.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurs are incentives or prompts to action, the same sense as stimuli.

clue.text: Apply authority without power

indicators.note: without says a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: an authority on a subject is an expert
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Use one's authority without having real power.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert pressure or influence is to apply it, as in applying force.

clue.text: Patriot arranged to host a very big singer

indicators.note: hosting takes guests inside, so these letters go within
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nationalist has organised a concert for a celebrated tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns PATRIOT into PAROTTI, which hosts A + V.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was a famous operatic tenor, large in both fame and build.

clue.text: Rector is touring old university, replacing another

parts.note: a rector and a vicar are both parish clergy

indicators.note: going round something, so these letters enclose the next ones

explanation.surface: A parish priest visits an ancient college, standing in for a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious means done or felt on behalf of someone else, acting in their place.

clue.text: Nut's not circular

definitions.meaning: describing an orbit or path that is off-centre

explanation.surface: The nut is not round.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric is an odd person, and eccentric orbits deviate from a perfect circle.

clue.text: Vineyard's two kinds of hot drink not common

parts.note: cha and tea are both words for the brewed drink
U means upper-class, as opposed to non-U or common

explanation.surface: The winery offers a couple of hot beverages and is rather posh.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U are old British labels for upper-class and common usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bordeaux a château is a wine estate, the vineyard and its house.

clue.text: Poles bring in cash over time, a tiny amount

indicators.note: bringing something in puts it inside the outer pair

parts.note: N and N, north being the abbreviation for a pole, here doubled

indicators.note: over is read as lying across, with the time letter dropped into the money

parts.note: the euro is a currency, so cash

explanation.surface: Polish workers earn money over a period, but only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like people from Poland. 'over' puts T into EURO; 'bring in' puts that between two Ns.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is a subatomic particle, about as small a quantity of matter as exists.

clue.text: Getting nearer after taking out very big stick

indicators.note: taking out says letters are removed from the word

parts.note: closing in means getting nearer
OS stands for outsize, a very large clothing size

explanation.surface: Approaching after pulling out an enormous stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to stick fast to something, as wet clothes adhere to skin.

clue.text: Officer left, intermittently eyeing Miss Ireland?

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel

indicators.note: on and off, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: An officer leaves, now and then looking at a beauty-contest winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Ireland looks like a pageant title; it means an Irish girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Colleen is an Irish word for a girl or young woman, a miss from Ireland.

clue.text: Unusually fierce English like salted roads

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An English person is oddly fierce, as on gritted winter streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt melts frost, so treated roads are clear of frozen water.

clue.text: More obscure work with a pair of rulers

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
QU and ER are both abbreviations for queen

explanation.surface: A darker task involving two monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means hard to see through or understand, so cloudier or murkier.

clue.text: Sierra and Golf's parting trip

indicators.note: parting splits something, so this letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a ride is a short journey
G is Golf in the NATO alphabet; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A NATO-alphabet pair, Sierra and Golf, take leave of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra looks like the NATO word for S; it is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged mountain range, a long elevated crest of high ground.

clue.text: Outstanding work on old shield in retreat

parts.note: RE means on or concerning

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a veil screens or shields

explanation.surface: A notable piece of craftsmanship on an ancient shield from a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: Outstanding means literally standing out from the surface. 'in retreat' turns OVEIL into LIEVO.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievo is relief sculpture, in which figures project from a flat background.

clue.text: Very embarrassed English prince stops act

indicators.note: stopping a gap fills it, so these letters plug the word

parts.note: a deed is an act

explanation.surface: An English prince interrupts a performance, to his mortification.
explanation.definitionFit: A very embarrassed face goes crimson, a blush of strong colour.

clue.text: Exceed two terms at Lord's

definitions.meaning: an over and a run are both cricket terms; Lord's is the London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Someone serves beyond the limit at a famous cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's best-known cricket ground; an over is six balls and a run a point scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go past a set limit of time or space.

clue.text: Elite insects regrouped with queen

indicators.note: regrouped means formed again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Superior bugs gather afresh around their queen, like a hive.
explanation.definitionFit: The quintessence is the purest, finest essence of something, hence its choicest part.
